nodes.name: Backing pump

properties.name: Backing pump
properties.description: Backing pump

evidence.text: During operation of the DRB, check the oil level and the condition of the oil in the oil level glass and the oiler from time to time. Correct as required (see Sections 6.3 and 6.4). Normally, the oil Tigol 100 is transparent. If it turns dark, this is a sign of early ageing due to excessively high temperatures. Run the DRB pump exclusively under the operating conditions for which it has been designed. Any modification of the operating parameters (e. g. intake pressure, intake temperature, ratio between DRB pump and backing pump) for a longer period may place an inadmissible thermal load on the pump.

Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must always be visible in the oiler (see Figure 11). The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. We recommend our vacuum pump oil Tigol 100. If it is required to top up oil very often, it is quite likely that a shaft seal is faulty.

nodes.name: Bearing spaces

properties.name: Bearing spaces
properties.description: Bearing spaces

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

nodes.name: Coupling halves

properties.name: Coupling halves
properties.description: Coupling halves

evidence.text: The bores in the coupling are manufactured to tolerance class H7, the shaft journals of the motor to tolerance class j6 resp. k6. The axial distance L1 (Figure 9) to the flange surface (area M in Figure 6) needs to be maintained according to the table. When not complying with this requirement there exists the likelihood of a mechanical contact and thus the creation of sparks between the coupling halves. Affix the coupling half with the M8 set screw, torque 10 Nm.

nodes.name: Coupling star

properties.name: Coupling star
properties.description: Coupling star

evidence.text: At the pump’s flange the respective studs have been preassembled, the washers and nuts which must be used have been enclosed with the pump. Check to ensure that the touch protection (Figure 7) has been correctly fitted in the pump’s flange. Insert the coupling star into the coupling half on the side of the pump. Align the coupling halves and push the motor on making sure that the flange surfaces run in parallel. Any tilt between motor axis anaxis can give rise to increased wear on the coupling star. Fit washers and nuts, and tighten according to the torque levels given in Figure 10.

nodes.name: Fan cowl

properties.name: Fan cowl
properties.description: Fan cowl

evidence.text: The slits in the fan cowl as well as the fins on the motor and on the pump may be contaminated depending on humidity conditions and the degree of contamination in the ambient air. In order to ensure a sufficient air flow for the motor and the pump’s casing, the grid of the fan cowl must be cleaned with a clean brush when contaminated. Any coarse dirt must be removed from the fins on the motor and the pump.

nodes.name: Intake dirt trap

properties.name: Intake dirt trap
properties.description: Intake dirt trap

evidence.text: A intake screen is located in the intake port to collect foreign objects. It should be kept clean in order to avoid a reduction of the pumping speed. To do so, take off the intake line. Remove the dirt trap from the intake flange and rinse it using a suitable solvent. Then thoroughly dry it with compressed air. If the dirt trap is damaged, replace it.

nodes.name: Pumping chamber

properties.name: Pumping chamber
properties.description: Pumping chamber

evidence.text: NOTE If the pump is not level, lubricant may enter the pumping chamber from the gear chambers.

Please consult us if you intend to run the pump with other oils or special lubricants. The oil filling levels stated in Figure 4 - which apply to the shutdown (standing still) pump - must be observed. The filling level visible in the oil-sight glass depends on the size of the pump and the type of oil used. If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high, oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. Clean the oil-fill port and reinstall the plug using a gasket which is in perfect condition. Wipe off any oil residues from the casing. The oil-fill port must be sealed air-tight.
In the presence of a vacuum, the entry of air may cause oil-containing gas to enter the pumping chamber via the rotor seals.

Under dirty operating conditions, contaminants may be deposited in the pumping chamber or on the rotors. After removing the two connecting lines, the contaminants can be blown out with dry compressed air or flushed out with a suitable solvent. Contaminants that cannot be blown or flushed out, can be removed completely from the pumping chamber with a wire brush, metallic sponge or scraper. Then change the oil.

nodes.name: Shaft seal
aliases: Outer shaft seal
Outer shaft sealing ring

properties.name: Shaft seal
properties.description: Shaft seal

evidence.text: Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must always be visible in the oiler (see Figure 11). The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. We recommend our vacuum pump oil Tigol 100. If it is required to top up oil very often, it is quite likely that a shaft seal is faulty.

When the oil level in the oiler drops and when oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the outer shaft seal is malfunctioning. If the oil loss is only slight, the pump may still be operated for some time, provided the lost oil is topped up regularly. Collect the oil which drips out under the motor. There is the danger that someone may slip. Have the pump repaired.

evidence.text:
Operation: Check oil quality | Meas./
Test quantity: Visual | Frequency: Weekly | Remark: In the normal state Tigol 100 is transparent. In the case of black oil an oil change is necessary, see Section 6.3.

Operation: Check oil quality | Meas./
Test quantity: Neutralization value (DIN 51 558) | Frequency: For normal operating conditions annually When pumping corrosive vapors, in the case of much dust and cyclic operation weekly to quarter yearly | Remark: If the neutralization value for Tigol 100 is > 2, then an oil change will be required, see Section 6.3.

Before pumping oxygen (or other highly reactive gases) at concentrations exceeding the concentration in the atmosphere (> 21 % for oxygen) it will be necessary to use a special pump. Such a pump will have to be modified and de-greased, and an inert special lubricant (e.g. PFPE) must be used. Very little oil is consumed by wear in the bearings and the gear under clean operating conditions. Under normal operating conditions, change the oil annually. Change the oil more frequently when pumping corrosive vapors or large amounts of dust or when cycling frequently from atmospheric to working pressure.

Under such operating conditions it is recommended to regularly check the neutralization value (to DIN 51 558) based on a sample of oil. If the neutralization value for Tigol 100 exceeds 2, an oil exchange will be required.

properties.instruction_text: Check rotor direction by briefly switching on the motor

evidence.text: After connecting the motor and every time you alter the wiring, check the direction of rotation.

WARNING Wear protective goggles for protection against particles which may be forced out of the flange opening. Keep your hands away from the flange opening. An arrow on the motor flange shows the correct direction of rotation for the rotor connected to the motor shaft (see Figure 2). To check rotation, switch on the motor briefly and observe the direction of rotor rotation through the pump’s intake and then immediately switch off again. The rotors should move up from the center and drop down to the side. If this is not the case, disconnect the pump from the mains and interchange two mains phases.

evidence.text: WARNING Wear protective goggles for protection against particles which may be forced out of the flange opening. Keep your hands away from the flange opening. An arrow on the motor flange shows the correct direction of rotation for the rotor connected to the motor shaft (see Figure 2). To check rotation, switch on the motor briefly and observe the direction of rotor rotation through the pump’s intake and then immediately switch off again. The rotors should move up from the center and drop down to the side. If this is not the case, disconnect the pump from the mains and interchange two mains phases.

Even if the pump has been already firmly connected to the piping, you may determine the direction of rotation. For this, evacuate the vacuum system down to a pressure below 20 mbar with the aid of the backing pump. Then switch on the DRB briefly; now the pressure must drop. If the pressure increases or remains constant, the DRB is turning in the wrong direction. Then rewire as described above.

evidence.text: WARNING During cleaning, the rotors must be turned only by hand. nodes.name: Have the pump repaired

properties.name: Have the pump repaired
properties.description: Have the pump repaired
properties.instruction_text: Have the pump repaired

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

When the oil level in the oiler drops and when oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the outer shaft seal is malfunctioning. If the oil loss is only slight, the pump may still be operated for some time, provided the lost oil is topped up regularly. Collect the oil which drips out under the motor. There is the danger that someone may slip. Have the pump repaired.

evidence.text: The housing for the shaft seal and the oiler are filled with oil when the pump is supplied. The oil level must be visible in the oiler. Correct oil level: 1/3 of the oiler must be filled when the pump is cold. Top up oil as required. The lubricant needed for running the pump is supplied in a separate container. Unscrew the oil-fill plug and add oil. Oil without additives and of viscosity class ISO VG 100 (formerly SAE 30) must be used for the pump. We recommend our special oil Tigol 100. Please consult us if you intend to run the pump with other oils or special lubricants. The oil filling levels stated in Figure 4 which apply to switch off pumps (at standstill) must be correctly maintained.

properties.instruction_text: Maintain the oil level at 1/3 of the oiler height when cold and 1/2 when warm

evidence.text: Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must always be visible in the oiler (see Figure 11). The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. We recommend our vacuum pump oil Tigol 100. If it is required to top up oil very often, it is quite likely that a shaft seal is faulty.

The slits in the fan cowl as well as the fins on the motor and on the pump may be contaminated depending on humidity conditions and the degree of contamination in the ambient air. nodes.name: Repair the pump for the faulty inner shaft seal

properties.name: Repair the pump for the faulty inner shaft seal
properties.description: Repair the pump for the faulty inner shaft seal
properties.instruction_text: Repair the pump for the faulty inner shaft seal

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

nodes.name: Rewire the DRB by interchanging two mains phases

properties.name: Rewire the DRB by interchanging two mains phases
properties.description: Rewire the DRB by interchanging two mains phases
properties.instruction_text: Rewire the DRB by interchanging two mains phases

evidence.text: WARNING Wear protective goggles for protection against particles which may be forced out of the flange opening. Keep your hands away from the flange opening. An arrow on the motor flange shows the correct direction of rotation for the rotor connected to the motor shaft (see Figure 2). To check rotation, switch on the motor briefly and observe the direction of rotor rotation through the pump’s intake and then immediately switch off again. The rotors should move up from the center and drop down to the side. If this is not the case, disconnect the pump from the mains and interchange two mains phases.

Even if the pump has been already firmly connected to the piping, you may determine the direction of rotation. For this, evacuate the vacuum system down to a pressure below 20 mbar with the aid of the backing pump. Then switch on the DRB briefly; now the pressure must drop. If the pressure increases or remains constant, the DRB is turning in the wrong direction. Then rewire as described above.

nodes.name: Run the DRB pump only under its designed operating conditions
aliases: Operate the DRB pump only under its designed operating conditions

properties.name: Run the DRB pump only under its designed operating conditions
properties.description: Run the DRB pump only under its designed operating conditions
properties.instruction_text: Run the DRB pump only under its designed operating conditions

evidence.text: During operation of the DRB, check the oil level and the condition of the oil in the oil level glass and the oiler from time to time. Correct as required (see Sections 6.3 and 6.4). Normally, the oil Tigol 100 is transparent. If it turns dark, this is a sign of early ageing due to excessively high temperatures. Run the DRB pump exclusively under the operating conditions for which it has been designed. Any modification of the operating parameters (e. g. intake pressure, intake temperature, ratio between DRB pump and backing pump) for a longer period may place an inadmissible thermal load on the pump.

Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must always be visible in the oiler (see Figure 11). The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. We recommend our vacuum pump oil Tigol 100. If it is required to top up oil very often, it is quite likely that a shaft seal is faulty.

If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high, oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. nodes.name: Use washers to equalize stress when bolting the pump feet down
aliases: Use washers to equalize stress when bolting down the pump feet

properties.name: Use washers to equalize stress when bolting the pump feet down
properties.description: Use washers to equalize stress when bolting the pump feet down
properties.instruction_text: Use washers to equalize stress when bolting the pump feet down

evidence.text: Keep the air intake and exhaust ducts for cooling the motor unobstructed (for minimum clearance with respect to the fan cowl, see Table 3). The pump’s ambient temperature should be between 12 °C and 40 °C. Lower temperatures hamper run-up; higher ones shorten the lubricant change intervals and may lead to greater wear. Special oil for operation at temperatures below 12 °C is available upon request. Secure the pump. Four holes in the feet are provided for this purpose. When bolting the feet down, make certain that there is no stress or twist on the pump casing.

Stress on the pump can change the close tolerances between the rotors and the pump casing and may result in damage to the pump (use washers to equalize). Since compensation elements must be attached to the flanges on the suction and pressure sides, the screws for attachment of the feet must always be fitted and tightened. Use the following screws: DRB 250/500 : 4 x M 12 DRB 1000/2000 : 4 x M 16

properties.description: Ambient temperature above 40 °C

evidence.text: Keep the air intake and exhaust ducts for cooling the motor unobstructed (for minimum clearance with respect to the fan cowl, see Table 3). The pump’s ambient temperature should be between 12 °C and 40 °C. Lower temperatures hamper run-up; higher ones shorten the lubricant change intervals and may lead to greater wear. Special oil for operation at temperatures below 12 °C is available upon request. Secure the pump. Four holes in the feet are provided for this purpose. When bolting the feet down, make certain that there is no stress or twist on the pump casing.

nodes.name: DRB turning in the wrong direction

properties.name: DRB turning in the wrong direction
properties.description: DRB turning in the wrong direction

evidence.text: WARNING Wear protective goggles for protection against particles which may be forced out of the flange opening. Keep your hands away from the flange opening. An arrow on the motor flange shows the correct direction of rotation for the rotor connected to the motor shaft (see Figure 2). To check rotation, switch on the motor briefly and observe the direction of rotor rotation through the pump’s intake and then immediately switch off again. The rotors should move up from the center and drop down to the side. If this is not the case, disconnect the pump from the mains and interchange two mains phases.

Even if the pump has been already firmly connected to the piping, you may determine the direction of rotation. For this, evacuate the vacuum system down to a pressure below 20 mbar with the aid of the backing pump. Then switch on the DRB briefly; now the pressure must drop. If the pressure increases or remains constant, the DRB is turning in the wrong direction. Then rewire as described above.

nodes.name: Faulty inner shaft seal

properties.name: Faulty inner shaft seal
properties.description: Faulty inner shaft seal

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

nodes.name: Oil level above the required level

evidence.text: Please consult us if you intend to run the pump with other oils or special lubricants. The oil filling levels stated in Figure 4 - which apply to the shutdown (standing still) pump - must be observed. The filling level visible in the oil-sight glass depends on the size of the pump and the type of oil used. If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high, oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. Clean the oil-fill port and reinstall the plug using a gasket which is in perfect condition. Wipe off any oil residues from the casing. The oil-fill port must be sealed air-tight.

evidence.text: During operation of the DRB, check the oil level and the condition of the oil in the oil level glass and the oiler from time to time. Correct as required (see Sections 6.3 and 6.4). Normally, the oil Tigol 100 is transparent. If it turns dark, this is a sign of early ageing due to excessively high temperatures. Run the DRB pump exclusively under the operating conditions for which it has been designed. Any modification of the operating parameters (e. g. intake pressure, intake temperature, ratio between DRB pump and backing pump) for a longer period may place an inadmissible thermal load on the pump.

nodes.name: Shaft seal is faulty
aliases: Faulty shaft seal

properties.name: Shaft seal is faulty
properties.description: Shaft seal is faulty

evidence.text: Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must always be visible in the oiler (see Figure 11). The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. We recommend our vacuum pump oil Tigol 100. If it is required to top up oil very often, it is quite likely that a shaft seal is faulty.

nodes.name: Stress or twist on the pump casing
aliases: Unspecified cause of stress or twist on the pump casing

properties.name: Stress or twist on the pump casing
properties.description: Stress or twist on the pump casing

evidence.text: Keep the air intake and exhaust ducts for cooling the motor unobstructed (for minimum clearance with respect to the fan cowl, see Table 3). The pump’s ambient temperature should be between 12 °C and 40 °C. Lower temperatures hamper run-up; higher ones shorten the lubricant change intervals and may lead to greater wear. Special oil for operation at temperatures below 12 °C is available upon request. Secure the pump. Four holes in the feet are provided for this purpose. When bolting the feet down, make certain that there is no stress or twist on the pump casing.

Stress on the pump can change the close tolerances between the rotors and the pump casing and may result in damage to the pump (use washers to equalize). Since compensation elements must be attached to the flanges on the suction and pressure sides, the screws for attachment of the feet must always be fitted and tightened. Use the following screws: DRB 250/500 : 4 x M 12 DRB 1000/2000 : 4 x M 16

nodes.name: Dropping oil level in the oiler with no oil under the shaft seal housing
aliases: Oil level drops in the oiler with no oil under the shaft seal housing

properties.name: Dropping oil level in the oiler with no oil under the shaft seal housing
properties.description: Dropping oil level in the oiler with no oil under the shaft seal housing

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

evidence.text: Keep the air intake and exhaust ducts for cooling the motor unobstructed (for minimum clearance with respect to the fan cowl, see Table 3). evidence.text: Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. nodes.name: Reduced pumping speed

properties.name: Reduced pumping speed
properties.description: Reduced pumping speed

evidence.text: A intake screen is located in the intake port to collect foreign objects. It should be kept clean in order to avoid a reduction of the pumping speed. To do so, take off the intake line. Remove the dirt trap from the intake flange and rinse it using a suitable solvent. Then thoroughly dry it with compressed air. If the dirt trap is damaged, replace it.

nodes.name: Rotor turns in the wrong direction

properties.name: Rotor turns in the wrong direction
properties.description: Rotor turns in the wrong direction

evidence.text: After connecting the motor and every time you alter the wiring, check the direction of rotation.

WARNING Wear protective goggles for protection against particles which may be forced out of the flange opening. Keep your hands away from the flange opening. An arrow on the motor flange shows the correct direction of rotation for the rotor connected to the motor shaft (see Figure 2). To check rotation, switch on the motor briefly and observe the direction of rotor rotation through the pump’s intake and then immediately switch off again. The rotors should move up from the center and drop down to the side. If this is not the case, disconnect the pump from the mains and interchange two mains phases.

Even if the pump has been already firmly connected to the piping, you may determine the direction of rotation. For this, evacuate the vacuum system down to a pressure below 20 mbar with the aid of the backing pump. Then switch on the DRB briefly; now the pressure must drop. If the pressure increases or remains constant, the DRB is turning in the wrong direction. Then rewire as described above.

evidence.text: Keep the air intake and exhaust ducts for cooling the motor unobstructed (for minimum clearance with respect to the fan cowl, see Table 3). The pump’s ambient temperature should be between 12 °C and 40 °C. Lower temperatures hamper run-up; higher ones shorten the lubricant change intervals and may lead to greater wear. Special oil for operation at temperatures below 12 °C is available upon request. Secure the pump. Four holes in the feet are provided for this purpose. evidence.text:
Operation: Check oil quality | Meas./
Test quantity: Neutralization value (DIN 51 558) | Frequency: For normal operating conditions annually When pumping corrosive vapors, in the case of much dust and cyclic operation weekly to quarter yearly | Remark: If the neutralization value for Tigol 100 is > 2, then an oil change will be required, see Section 6.3.

nodes.name: Unacceptably high oil level in the pump bearing spaces

properties.name: Unacceptably high oil level in the pump bearing spaces
properties.description: Unacceptably high oil level in the pump bearing spaces

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

conditions.text: If the oil level is too low
If the oil level is too low

notes: one end is not named in the source

evidence.text: The housing for the shaft seal and the oiler are filled with oil when the pump is supplied. The oil level must be visible in the oiler. Correct oil level: 1/3 of the oiler must be filled when the pump is cold. Top up oil as required. The lubricant needed for running the pump is supplied in a separate container. Unscrew the oil-fill plug and add oil. Oil without additives and of viscosity class ISO VG 100 (formerly SAE 30) must be used for the pump. We recommend our special oil Tigol 100. Please consult us if you intend to run the pump with other oils or special lubricants. The oil filling levels stated in Figure 4 which apply to switch off pumps (at standstill) must be correctly maintained.

If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. Clean the oil-fill port and screw the plug back in using a gasket which is in perfect condition. The oil-fill port must be sealed air-tight. Entry of air from the outside may cause oil-containing gas to enter the pumping chamber via the rotors seals.

To check rotation, switch on the motor briefly and observe the direction of rotor rotation through the pump’s intake and then immediately switch off again. The rotors should move up from the center and drop down to the side. If this is not the case, disconnect the pump from the mains and interchange two mains phases.

Even if the pump has been already firmly connected to the piping, you may determine the direction of rotation. For this, evacuate the vacuum system down to a pressure below 20 mbar with the aid of the backing pump. Then switch on the DRB briefly; now the pressure must drop. If the pressure increases or remains constant, the DRB is turning in the wrong direction. Then rewire as described above.

Fit washers and nuts, and tighten according to the torque levels given in Figure 10.

evidence.text: During operation of the DRB, check the oil level and the condition of the oil in the oil level glass and the oiler from time to time. Correct as required (see Sections 6.3 and 6.4). Normally, the oil Tigol 100 is transparent. If it turns dark, this is a sign of early ageing due to excessively high temperatures. Run the DRB pump exclusively under the operating conditions for which it has been designed. Any modification of the operating parameters (e. g. intake pressure, intake temperature, ratio between DRB pump and backing pump) for a longer period may place an inadmissible thermal load on the pump.

evidence.text: WARNING Do not operate the pump without having connected the flanges to a vacuum system The screws of the flanges on the suction and the pressure side must not be loosened in the presence of a vacuum even if the pump is not running.
WARNING
Hot surfaces, risk of suffering burns. Notice safety information 0.3.

During operation of the DRB, check the oil level and the condition of the oil in the oil level glass and the oiler from time to time. Correct as required (see Sections 6.3 and 6.4). Normally, the oil Tigol 100 is transparent. If it turns dark, this is a sign of early ageing due to excessively high temperatures. Run the DRB pump exclusively under the operating conditions for which it has been designed. Any modification of the operating parameters (e. g. intake pressure, intake temperature, ratio between DRB pump and backing pump) for a longer period may place an inadmissible thermal load on the pump.

Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must always be visible in the oiler (see Figure 11). The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. We recommend our vacuum pump oil Tigol 100. If it is required to top up oil very often, it is quite likely that a shaft seal is faulty.

WARNING Before removing the oil-drain or oil-fill plug always switch off the pump first and vent to atmospheric pressure. When the pump has become warm during operation, the casing and the oil temperature may exceed 80 ºC. Leave the pump to cool down. Always wear protective gloves also to protect yourself against aggressive residues in the oil.

Before pumping oxygen (or other highly reactive gases) at concentrations exceeding the concentration in the atmosphere (> 21 % for oxygen) it will be necessary to use a special pump. Such a pump will have to be modified and de-greased, and an inert special lubricant (e.g. PFPE) must be used. Very little oil is consumed by wear in the bearings and the gear under clean operating conditions. Under normal operating conditions, change the oil annually. Change the oil more frequently when pumping corrosive vapors or large amounts of dust or when cycling frequently from atmospheric to working pressure.

Under such operating conditions it is recommended to regularly check the neutralization value (to DIN 51 558) based on a sample of oil. If the neutralization value for Tigol 100 exceeds 2, an oil exchange will be required.

Change the oil more frequently when pumping corrosive vapors or large amounts of dust or when cycling frequently from atmospheric to working pressure.

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

evidence.text: 6.9 Exchanging the Shaft Seals

The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.
6.9.1 Preparations

(See Figure 14 and 15). Pull the shaft seal housing out. Forcing threads are provided on the shaft seal housing for this purpose. Take the O-ring out of the flange of the coupling. Use a puller to pull the bushing off from the shaft. Take the O-ring from the shaft.

evidence.text: After connecting the motor and every time you alter the wiring, check the direction of rotation.

WARNING Wear protective goggles for protection against particles which may be forced out of the flange opening. Keep your hands away from the flange opening. An arrow on the motor flange shows the correct direction of rotation for the rotor connected to the motor shaft (see Figure 2). To check rotation, switch on the motor briefly and observe the direction of rotor rotation through the pump’s intake and then immediately switch off again. The rotors should move up from the center and drop down to the side. If this is not the case, disconnect the pump from the mains and interchange two mains phases.

Even if the pump has been already firmly connected to the piping, you may determine the direction of rotation. For this, evacuate the vacuum system down to a pressure below 20 mbar with the aid of the backing pump. Then switch on the DRB briefly; now the pressure must drop. If the pressure increases or remains constant, the DRB is turning in the wrong direction. Then rewire as described above.

The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.
